intro: The meter bus of heat, water and gas meters in Europe (EN 13757). A master, here the data collector, powers a pair of wires and asks each meter in turn. The meter answers with a header (its ID, maker and type) and data records. Each record says what it measures and in which unit. Wireless M-Bus sends the same records by radio, without being asked.
plain: Many buildings have a heat, water or gas meter in every apartment. The meter bus connects them all to one collector box with a single pair of wires, which also powers them. The box calls each meter in turn, like a teacher calling roll, and each one answers with its readings. Meters without a wire send their readings by radio instead, scrambled so that only someone with the right key can read them.

reset.title: Reset the link
reset.text: The collector sends SND_NKE ("reset your link") to primary address 5: a short number, set on each meter, that names it on this bus. The meter answers with one byte, E5, which means OK. The bus runs at 2400 baud (bits per second), with 8 data bits and an even parity bit that catches single-bit errors.

ask.title: Ask for data
ask.text: REQ_UD2 (request user data) asks the heat meter for its data. One bit in it, the frame count bit (FCB), tells a new request from a repeated one. After a reset, the first request must carry FCB 1.

answer.title: The data records
answer.text: The meter answers with a long frame, called a telegram: a fixed header, then data records. Each record starts with a DIF (data information field: how the value is coded) and a VIF (value information field: what it is, and in which unit). The value follows. The last byte before the checksum, 0x1F, says: more in the next telegram.

next.title: The next telegram
next.text: The collector flips the FCB, from 1 to 0, and asks again. The meter sends its second telegram: the values stored on the last due date, the day the utility bills on.

radio.title: Wireless M-Bus
radio.text: The water meter has no wire to the bus. Every 16 seconds it sends its values by radio, encrypted with AES-128, a standard cipher. Each meter has its own key, so the collector needs this meter's key to read them.

frames.rsp-1: Heat 12 345 kWh, volume 456.78 m³, flow 70.2 °C and return 45.3 °C, more to come

notes.wmbus: Nobody asked: a meter in T1 mode only sends, it never listens. In clear come the length, C-field 0x44 (SND_NR: send, no reply), the maker EXA, the ID 87654321, a version and the type 0x07 (water). Then CI 0x7A, with an access number, a status byte and a configuration word that says mode 5: AES-128 in CBC mode. The rest is encrypted. The IV, the starting value of the encryption, is built from the maker, the address and the access number. The key belongs to this one meter. Decrypted, the data starts with 2F 2F, then DIF and VIF records like the wired ones. Every block of the frame has its own CRC. On air, each 4 bits travel as 6 chips (the 3-out-of-6 code).

short.name: Start
short.note: 0x10 starts a short frame: 5 bytes in all.

c-nke.name: C-field 0x40
c-nke.note: SND_NKE: reset the link. The meter clears its frame count bit.

a-5.name: Address 5
a-5.note: The meter's primary address. 1 to 250 are for meters, and a new meter answers at 0. 253 means: use the secondary address (the ID) instead. 254 and 255 reach every meter.

cs-nke.name: Checksum
cs-nke.note: 0x45 = 0x40 + 0x05: the sum of C and A, modulo 256 (only the last 8 bits are kept).

c-req-1.name: C-field 0x7B
c-req-1.note: REQ_UD2: send me your user data. The frame count bit (0x20) is 1: the first request after a reset carries FCB 1.

long-42.name: Start
long-42.note: A long frame: 0x68, the length twice, 0x68 again. 0x2A = 42 bytes from C to the last data byte.

ci.name: CI-field 0x72
ci.note: Variable data: first a long header, then records of any type and length. Numbers come low byte first.

id.name: ID number
id.note: 12345678 in BCD (two decimal digits in each byte), low byte first. It is printed on the meter, and it is its secondary address.

maker.name: Maker
maker.note: 0x1701 = EXA, a made-up code: three letters packed into 15 bits (taken apart below).

version.name: Version
version.note: 1: the version of this meter type.

medium.name: Medium
medium.note: 0x04: heat, with the flow sensor in the return pipe. 0x07 is water, 0x03 gas.

access-42.name: Access number
access-42.note: 0x2A = 42. It goes up by one with every answer.

access-43.name: Access number
access-43.note: 0x2B = 43: one more than the last answer.

energy.name: Energy
energy.note: DIF 0x0C: 8 BCD digits. VIF 0x06: energy in kWh. 00012345 = 12 345 kWh.

volume.name: Volume
volume.note: DIF 0x0C. VIF 0x14: volume in steps of 0.01 m³. 00045678 = 456.78 m³.

flow.name: Flow temperature
flow.note: DIF 0x0A: 4 BCD digits. VIF 0x5A: flow temperature (the hot water coming in) in steps of 0.1 °C. 0702 = 70.2 °C.

return.name: Return temperature
return.note: VIF 0x5E: return temperature (the cooler water going back) in steps of 0.1 °C. 0453 = 45.3 °C.

now.name: Date and time
now.note: DIF 0x04: a 32-bit value. VIF 0x6D: date and time (type F), packed into bits: 2026-11-12 08:15.

more.name: More
more.note: DIF 0x1F: more records follow in the next telegram.

cs-rsp-1.name: Checksum
cs-rsp-1.note: 0xA1: the sum of every byte from C to the last data byte, modulo 256.

c-req-2.name: C-field 0x5B
c-req-2.note: REQ_UD2 with FCB 0. The bit changed, so the meter sends its next telegram. With the same bit, it would send the last one again.

long-31.name: Start
long-31.note: 0x1F = 31 bytes from C to the last data byte.

due-date.name: Due date
due-date.note: DIF 0x42: storage 1 (a stored value), 16 bits. VIF 0x6C: a date (type G): 2025-12-31.

due-energy.name: Energy on the due date
due-energy.note: DIF 0x4C: storage 1, 8 BCD digits. VIF 0x06: kWh. 00009876 = 9 876 kWh.

due-volume.name: Volume on the due date
due-volume.note: DIF 0x4C, VIF 0x14: storage 1, in steps of 0.01 m³. 00038123 = 381.23 m³.

cs-rsp-2.name: Checksum
cs-rsp-2.note: 0x6B: the sum from C to the last data byte.

d-extension.name: Extension
d-extension.note: 0: no DIFE byte follows. DIFEs (DIF extensions) add bits for higher storage numbers, tariffs and subunits.

d-storage.name: Storage number
d-storage.note: 1. 0 is the value now; higher numbers are stored values. In this meter, 1 is the last due date.

d-function.name: Function
d-function.note: 00: an instantaneous value. 01 is a maximum, 10 a minimum, 11 a value during an error.

d-data.name: Data field
d-data.note: 1100: 8 BCD digits, in 4 bytes. 0100 would be a 32-bit integer.

facts.between: Data collector (master) → heat, water, gas and electricity meters
facts.transport: Two wires, powered by the master, 2400 baud 8E1; radio at 868 MHz (T1: 868.95 MHz)
facts.security: Wired: usually none, though the same encryption can be switched on. Wireless: AES-128 with a key for each meter (mode 5 or 7)
facts.frames: E5: acknowledge · 10 … 16: short frame · 68 L L 68 … 16: long frame

tips: Every meter on the bus needs its own primary address. New meters answer at 0, and two of them at 0 garble each other. Set the address first, or address meters by their ID number (secondary addressing).
Flip the FCB only to get the next telegram. A collector that never flips it reads telegram 1 again and again, and never sees the stored values.
Take the unit from the VIF of every record. 0x13 is liters, 0x14 tens of liters: copying the scaling from another meter type makes bills ten times off.
Ask the supplier for each wireless meter's AES key with the delivery. Without it, the collector sees the ID and the type, but no value.

timing.title: How bits travel on the two wires
timing.note: SND_NKE from the master, then E5 from the meter. The master signals with voltage: about 36 V for a 1, 12 V less for a 0. The meter signals with current: 1.5 mA for a 1, 11 to 20 mA more for a 0. So the same two wires carry power and data both ways. Each character is 11 bits: a start bit, 8 data bits (lowest first), even parity and a stop bit. At 2400 baud, a bit lasts 0.42 ms.

anatomy.maker: The maker's code, packed into two bytes

playground.file: Try it: the heat meter's records as the collector decodes them, one per line.
playground.layout: Each record: the DIF says how the data is stored, the VIF what it measures and in which unit, then the data, least significant byte first.
playground.energy: DIF 0C: 8 digits in BCD. VIF 06: energy in kWh. Read the bytes backwards: 00 01 23 45, so 12345.
playground.volume: VIF 14: volume in steps of 0.01 m³: 00045678 × 0.01 = 456.78 m³.
playground.flow: DIF 0A: 4 digits in BCD. VIF 5A: flow temperature in steps of 0.1 °C: 0702, so 70.2 °C.
playground.return: VIF 5E: return temperature, also in 0.1 °C. The difference with the flow, times the water that passed, is the heat delivered.
playground.due: DIF 4C: storage 1, the value saved on the due date: the one the bill uses.
playground.encoder: Some meters send a binary integer (DIF 04, 32 bits) instead of BCD: its bytes too come least significant first (DCBA). Type a value to see them.
